_meta.note: verbatim fields contain exact captured output. commentary fields contain human interpretation.

wrapperFormat.commentary: Each tool result is wrapped in a <result> block with <name> identifying the tool and either <output> for success or <error> for failure. When multiple tools are called in parallel, results appear as multiple <result> blocks. A <system-reminder> block with token count may be appended after results.

full_file.verbatim:
1	Line 1: Greetings, Universe! ...
2	Line 2: ...
...
20	Line 20: Final line with trailing newline.
21
full_file.commentary: Output uses cat -n format: line_number TAB content. Line numbers start at 1. Blank lines show just the line number and tab. Empty trailing line (line 21) indicates file ends with newline.

partial_with_offset_limit.commentary: Same cat -n format. offset=5 starts at line 5, limit=3 returns 3 lines (5, 6, 7).

file_not_found.verbatim: File does not exist. Note: your current working directory is C:\AI\MOSAIC\MOSAIC.
file_not_found.commentary: Returned via <error> wrapper instead of <output>. Includes the current working directory as context.

large_file_default_truncation.verbatim:
1	foxtrot golf [ROW:0001] hotel india
...
1518	foxtrot golf [ROW:1518] hotel india

<system-reminder>
[Truncated: PARTIAL view — ...large-file-3000-lines.txt: showing lines 1-1518 of 3001 total (42006 tokens, cap 25000). Call Read with offset=1519 limit=1518 for the next page, or Grep to find a specific section. Do NOT answer from this page alone if the answer may be further in the file.]
</system-reminder>
large_file_default_truncation.commentary: Default read limit is 2000 lines per the tool description, but actual truncation is token-based (cap 25000 tokens). For this file, truncation occurred at line 1518 of 3001 total. A system-reminder is injected with truncation details including: lines shown, total lines, token count, token cap, and pagination instructions.

new_file.verbatim: File created successfully at: C:\Users\tgurt\AppData\Local\Temp\...\write-test.txt (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)
new_file.commentary: Success message includes full absolute path and a reminder not to re-read the file.

success.call: Edit({file_path: 'edit-test-copy.txt', old_string: 'Line 16: Swap this line with different content.', new_string: 'Line 16: EDITED SUCCESSFULLY by capture agent.'})
success.verbatim: The file ...\edit-test-copy.txt has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)
success.commentary: Success message includes full path and reminder not to re-read.

old_string_not_found.call: Edit({file_path: 'edit-test-copy.txt', old_string: 'THIS STRING DOES NOT EXIST IN THE FILE', new_string: 'replacement text'})
old_string_not_found.verbatim:
<error><tool_use_error>String to replace not found in file.
String: THIS STRING DOES NOT EXIST IN THE FILE</tool_use_error></error>
old_string_not_found.commentary: Error is wrapped in <error><tool_use_error> tags (not just <error>). Includes the string that was not found.

success.commentary: Plain stdout content returned via <output> wrapper. No exit code shown on success.

error_nonzero_exit.verbatim:
Exit code 127
/usr/bin/bash: line 1: nonexistent_command_xyz_12345: command not found
error_nonzero_exit.commentary: Returned via <error> wrapper. First line is 'Exit code {N}', followed by stderr content.

long_output.commentary: All 5000 lines returned in full with no truncation. Bash does not appear to have a default output line limit — but a system-reminder with token count may be appended.

no_output.call: Bash({command: 'cp source dest'}) — command with no stdout
no_output.commentary: When a command succeeds but produces no stdout, the harness returns this specific message instead of empty output.

with_matches.commentary: Matching file paths listed one per line, using backslash separators on Windows. Paths are relative to the working directory.

no_matches.commentary: Specific message when no files match the pattern.

content_mode_with_matches.commentary: Format is file_path:line_number:matching_line_content. Uses backslash path separators on Windows.

no_matches.commentary: Specific message when no content matches the pattern.

with_glob_filter.commentary: Same format as without glob filter. The glob parameter restricts which files are searched.

not_captured.commentary: Agent tool is available in subagent context but spawning a test subagent is only done in PrimaryAgent tier per the capture guide.
TaskStop requires a running background task ID. No task was spawned to exercise this tool against.

not_available.commentary: AskUserQuestion is not a built-in tool in the subagent context. The MCP server 'contact-user' provides ask_user_questions via MCP, but MCP tools are excluded from this capture.
